title: The Global Race for Lunar Resource Exploration
subtitle: An examination of the legal, technical, and geopolitical challenges surrounding the extraction of resources on the Moon.
description: As nations and private companies set their sights on the Moon's mineral and water resources, the world faces a new frontier of competition. This series explores the shift from scientific exploration to industrial exploitation and the implications for international law.

articles.label: Part 1
articles.note: The transition from Cold War-era exploration to modern resource-driven interest, focusing on the discovery of lunar water ice.

articles.label: Part 2
articles.note: The roles of state-led agencies (NASA, CNSA) versus private sector entities (SpaceX, Blue Origin).

articles.label: Part 3
articles.note: The conflict between the 1967 Outer Space Treaty and modern commercial extraction ambitions.

articles.label: Part 4
articles.note: The economic implications of a lunar supply chain and the potential for a new 'space race' to impact Earth-based industries.

articles.label: Part 5
articles.note: The need for a new international framework to manage lunar resources and prevent conflict.
